title: What decimal do these quantities make?
description: Quantities made from several places are changed into one decimal, following the book's example. A last step splits the first answer by places again.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn each place into its value and add. Watch for children who write a count of ten or more in one place without carrying it.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q14
video_script.why: The child has written quantities with one digit per place and now meets counts of ten or more in a place.
video_script.substitution: Turn each place into its value, then add the values.
video_script.anchor: three quantities made from several places
video_script.payoff_line: Turn each place into its value, then add them up

final_answer.spoken: one hundred twenty-one point two, one hundred eleven point one and two hundred seventy-seven point seven five

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths and hundredths are said as words
maths_rules: example: 87 + 0.5 + 0.60 = 88.10, since 60 hundredths = 6 tenths and 5 tenths + 6 tenths = 1.1
check: 121.2 has 12 tens, and 1 unit + 2 tenths = 12 tenths
video_script.design: The three quantities stay in the anchor band; the book's example opens the stage, each quantity is turned into values and added in the working band, and a last step splits 121.2 by places.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three quantities (a) 12 tens and 12 tenths (b) 10 tens, 10 ones, 10 tenths and 10 hundredths (c) 25 tens, 25 ones, 25 tenths and 25 hundredths; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about building a number from many places.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Three quantities are given, each made from several different places.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each one as a single decimal, like the book's example.

beats.on_screen: the quantities stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the book's example: 87 ones, 5 tenths and 60 hundredths; 60 hundredths = 6 tenths; 5 tenths + 6 tenths = 1 unit and 1 tenth; 88.10

marks.sum: 5 tenths + 6 tenths = 1 unit and 1 tenth, and 88.10 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>The book's example is eighty-seven ones, five tenths and sixty hundredths.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Sixty hundredths is six tenths, and five tenths plus six tenths is one unit and one tenth.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The example then makes eighty-eight point one zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: 12 tens and 12 tenths; 10 tens, 10 ones, 10 tenths and 10 hundredths; 25 tens, 25 ones, 25 tenths and 25 hundredths
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, twelve tens and twelve tenths.
Also ten of each of four places, and then twenty-five of each.

beats.on_screen: To find: each quantity as one decimal
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each quantity as one decimal.

marks.a: 12 tens is changed to 120 and 12 tenths to 1.2

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, twelve tens is one hundred twenty, and twelve tenths is one point two.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>We add them and get one hundred twenty-one point two.

marks.b1: 10 tens is changed to 100 and 10 ones to 10
marks.b2: 10 tenths is changed to 1 and 10 hundredths to 0.1

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step two, ten tens is a hundred, and ten ones is ten.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Ten tenths is one, and ten hundredths is zero point one.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Added together, they give one hundred eleven point one.

marks.c1: 25 tens is changed to 250 and 25 ones to 25
marks.c2: 25 tenths is changed to 2.5 and 25 hundredths to 0.25

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, twenty-five tens is two hundred fifty, and twenty-five ones is twenty-five.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Twenty-five tenths is two point five, and twenty-five hundredths is zero point two five.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Added together, they give two hundred seventy-seven point seven five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check 121.2 by places: 1 hundred + 2 tens = 12 tens; 1 unit + 2 tenths = 12 tenths

marks.same: 12 tens and 12 tenths are matched to the question

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, put the first answer back by splitting one hundred twenty-one point two by places.
<bookmark mark='same'/>It has twelve tens, and one unit and two tenths make twelve tenths.

marks.first: the first two answers are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Turn each place into its value, then add them up.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two are one hundred twenty-one point two and one hundred eleven point one.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last is two hundred seventy-seven point seven five.
